summary:
# NOTES: *The Emblems of Fidelity: A Comedy in Letters* (James Lane Allen, 1919, Doubleday, Page & Co.)

**Form:** Epistolary comedy, ~70 letters/diary entries in 3 sections (Pt 1 1910; Pt 2 1911; Pt 3 1912). Frontmatter: epigraph from Chesterfield on audible laughter ("nobody has ever heard me laugh"). Dedication: "To THE SPIRIT OF COMEDY, Incomparable Ally of Victory." Sections: PART SECOND, PART THIRD.

## Characters
- **Edward Blackthorne**: famous elderly English novelist, King Alfred's Wood, Warwickshire. Vain ("elephant proboscis" for praise, "greyhound" for compliments). Wife (Mrs. Blackthorne) unnamed. Loves ferns (fern bank). Wrote "Black Oaks" grove. Secretary: Anne Raeburn. Dogs. Gardener: Hodge.
- **Beverley Sands**: rising young American novelist, Kentucky stories, lives Cathedral Heights, NY. Age 27 in 1910. Fiancé of Tilly. Dictates novels. Diarist.
- **Benjamin "Ben" Doolittle**: practical lawyer, Beverley's friend. Office 150 Broad St, later 150 Wall St. "Land-turtle" (no imagination). Fiancé/lover of Polly. Signs "Your obliged counsel and turtle." Later "Sal Blivvens" (Blackthorne's jibe).
- **George Marigold** (Dr. G. M. Marigold): fashionable physician. Tilly's doctor; marries Tilly July 1912.
- **Claude Mullen**: fashionable nerve specialist, Marigold's friend. "Giraffe-headed jackass" (Ben). Loved Polly; she married him July 1912.
- **Rufus Kent**: long-winded president of The Great Dipper club; "Nestor."
- **Noah Chamberlain**: professor of botany, Seminole, NC; absent-minded; "Approximations to Consciousness in Plants" (unfinished). Dies after fall down library steps (~Dec 1911), pneumonia.
- **Clara Louise Chamberlain**: his daughter, secretary; "proud daughter of the Southland"; devoted, bitter. Later greenhouse worker for Andy Peters; then NY job seeker.
- **Tilly Snowden**: Beverley's sweetheart; "Slippery Elm" Apartments; wild-rose-in-snowbank; six sisters family; "long love is possible only when you love often."
- **Polly Boles**: Ben's sweetheart, Tilly's friend; Franklin Flats; loyal; "indispensable."
- **Florists**: Phillips & Faulds (Louisville, Ky.; Ben's old florist; did not pay debts); Burns & Bruce (Dunkirk, Tenn.; native fern collectors); Judd & Judd ("Per Q."; NY landscape architects); Andy Peters (Seminole, NC; married Alice, July 1912).
- **Hodge**: Blackthorne's stupid gardener; claims age 58; scrapes neck with thumb; hates Latin fern names; murders ferns (scrapes soil, jabs trowel). Dies July 1912 ("birthday eclipse").

## PART ONE

**1. Blackthorne → Sands, King Alfred's Wood, May 1, 1910.** Praises Kentucky novel. Stableman/horse/oats/halter metaphor ("you are my animal"). Wants root-stocks of Kentucky ferns for fern bank. Backstory: Corot's trees look like ferns; dug Corot ferns; Christine Nilsson (Covent Garden) sent Norwegian ferns in memory of Balzac and *Seraphita*; Turgenieff in Paris: quoted passage ("splendid clear morning… songs of larks"); "What is it you definitely missed?" "Ferns." Turgenieff: "That spot is all Russia!" Hamper of Russian fern-roots with Turgenieff's card. "Pounds sterling… transaction of the market-place."

**2. Sands → Blackthorne, Cathedral Heights, May 12, 1910.** Letter "unreal" (whale/porpoise fable; oak/dogwood). Reads all his books. Says praise "too late, in bad taste." Shakespeare's bosom joke. Will ship ferns; encloses catalogues; asks for list.

**3. Blackthorne → Sands, May 22, 1910.** Hinges paradox ("climb our mountain by walking away"). Encloses fern list; cost ~£5 ("fifty guineas" joke). Wooden slab headstones (Hodge reads Latin). Hodge described as "English landscape gardening in human shape," "two-legged god." Hodge announces "*Asplenium filix-faemina*… Bishop's crooks." Visitors' stroll: Hodge answers "*Polydactulum cruciato-cristatum*, sir"; "*Polypodium elegantissimum*, mum." Foreign ferns die; Hodge suspected of murder ("Hodge's spot"). Two pleadings: British patriotism; Latin resistance. Mrs. Blackthorne "charmed." Invites Sands and wife-to-be to garden. Proboscis "like a gun-barrel" toward US. Signed "Your deeply interested."

**4. Sands → Tilly, June 3 (1910).** "Crown me with slippery elm." Blackthorne invitation to "Mrs. Beverley Sands." Imagines English tea, Sandringham, Stonehenge tea under umbrellas. "Future honours" as her estate. "Miss Snowden" persists. Proposes "Madame Snowden" name. Tilly's remark: two protracted pleasures (engagement, marriage). Asks about her health; fears "Doctor G. M." Signed "Your easy and your uneasy BEVERLEY."

**5. Tilly → Sands, "Slippery Elm" Apts, June 4.** Refuses "creative hair" (literary honours). Childhood memory: mother's friend, minister's wife; turkey/ducks; "strip of territory" beside Canaan; husband = Canaan. Admits postponing marriage. P.S.: wants England; "I am now a patient" of Dr. Marigold; "mild auto-intoxication"; will take "Bulgar bacillus." Asks why Beverley dislikes Marigold. Signed "auto-intoxicated, not otherwise intoxicated!"

**6. Sands → Ben, June 3.** "Bolt of divine lightning." Blackthorne praise. Ben doesn't read fiction; read *Ten Thousand a Year*. Land-turtle/carapace/five senses. Asks for Louisville florist address. "Naught that makes life most worth while can be had for gold." P.S. asks about Polly; "Predestined magpies!"

**7. Ben → Sands, June 5.** Quotes "*A chaque oiseau / Son nid est beau*." Denies ever trafficking in ferns. Calls Beverley "a poor, harmless tinker"; sign "Tinkering done here." Lawyer's view: imagination is "polecat of the human faculties." Recommends Phillips & Faulds ("opossum with hyacinths"). Signed "your obliged counsel and turtle." P.S. "Uncertain doves!"

**8. Ben → Polly, June 5.** Red roses. Asks Polly to thank him, name visit day, give Louisville florist address, explain patience with Mullen. Signed "Thy sworn and thy swain."

**9. Polly → Ben, Franklin Flats, June 6.** Calls request "flimsiest subterfuge." Louisville florists sent "not fresh" flowers; Phillips & Faulds sent "biggest boxes." Appointment tomorrow; will "divide the evening." Mullen loves her; she doesn't ("his lower eyelids… cupfuls of sentimental fluid"). Signed "indispensable."

**10. Polly → Tilly, June 6.** Asks Tilly to come early/divide evening; "Why not let him suffer awhile?" P.S.: postpone altogether.

**11. Tilly → Polly, June 6.** Sees through. Parlour as "enormous turnip" (beets, horse-radish, wilted electric sunflower). Loyalty as "vampire trait." Franklin Flats memory: "Beware of meat twice boiled"/"good restaurant." "Strictly Monogamous Women" banner vs her "Not Necessarily Monogamous!" Barefoot vs goloshes. Announces she will marry Beverley. Blackthorne invited them "to bring me along." Tells Polly she is Marigold's patient. Encloses Beverley's letter (Beverley furious). "Disloyalty… for the sake of loyalty to Ben."

**12. Polly → Tilly, June 7.** Returns Beverley letter unread. Defends Beverley. Says Tilly "courts irresponsibility." Final jab: nature left out Tilly's "domestic tea-kettle," "overdoing the stove."

**13. Sands → Phillips & Faulds, dated "June 7, 1900" [sic; 1910 intended].** Orders Kentucky ferns, $25 check, ship to Blackthorne. **P&F reply, Louisville, June 10, 1900 [sic]:** "We handle most of the ferns."

**14. Sands → Blackthorne, June 15, 1910.** "Argosy" letter. Delay due to fern shipping. "Dilemma of my life": Mrs. Sands "exists" but "there is no such person." Peach/bough image. Asks to come alone if Tilly undecided. P.S.: marriage denied due to feminism; "shadow" and "penumbra" speech.

**15. Diary of Beverley Sands, June 16 (1910).** Blackthorne read novel; ferns praised. Tilly's "golden balances." Polly's Bohemian supper ("aux sardines") at Franklin Flats. Ben softening. Publisher "human refrigerator." Club president congratulates loudly; two charlatans (Marigold, Mullen) with dark looks. **Confession: "There was no woodland scene and there were no ferns."** Real origin: at 17, August afternoon, walking home in Kentucky, dry spring, sycamore shade, butterflies, grasshopper; imagined the scene while writing.

## PART TWO

**16. Blackthorne → Sands, May 1, 1911.** "DEAR SIR." Says Sands broke bond (no ferns). Analogies: cabbage, oak, grape-vine, plover, quartz crystallisation ("powers of crystallisation"; "memory is a millstream"). Ancient emblem: "The fern stood for Fidelity." Shadow on the garden spot and on his shelves where Sands's books were. "Specious books… successful scamps."

**17. Sands → Blackthorne, May 10, 1911.** Cold: "I have never felt called upon to defend my character. Nor will I… attack your character."

**18. Sands → Ben, May 13, 1911.** Encloses letters. Louisville firm cashed check. Blackthorne's "insult." Pearl and pearl-owner. Tilly must have "the spring" of her hopes; Balzac's *The Magic Skin*: Sands is "shrinking skin" to Tilly. Signed "(the Expanding Scamp and the Shrinking Skin)."

**19. Ben → Sands, May 14.** "Fie, fee, fo, fum." Keeps documents in locker with Sands's "immortal but impecunious Will." Calls Blackthorne "aged book-skunk," "polecat." Shark-fish story. Warns about Tilly.

**20. Phillips & Faulds → Sands, May 13, 1911.** Senior member ill; order passed to Burns & Bruce; debts; junior member's marriage; litigation. "Your letter is pretty rough."

**21. Burns & Bruce → Sands, Dunkirk, Tenn., May 20, 1911.** Drought, frost; ferns withered; P&F "not good paying." Recommends **Noah Chamberlain, Seminole, NC**, "authority on American ferns."

**22. Sands → Ben, May 24.** P&F letter "cold purity of a whitewashed rotten Kentucky fence." Wants suit. "Thus I now press on over the Tennessee state line into North Carolina."

**23. Sands → Noah Chamberlain, May 25, 1911.** Order, $25 check.

**24. Noah → Sands, Seminole, May 29.** "I am not a florist." Professor of botany 15 yrs. Friend: President of Royal Botanical Society of Great Britain.

**25. Clara → Sands, May 29.** Indignant. Compares father to Dana, Gray, Humboldt. "You must be some kind of nonentity." Check returned.

**26. Sands → Noah, June 3.** Mocking apology: "you may be merely a famous liar." Asks return of list. Signed "BEVERLEY SANDS, A.B. (merely)."

**27. Noah → Sands, June 8.** "I know nothing about any list of ferns. Stop writing to me."

**28. Clara → Sands, June 8.** "What a viper." Father couldn't eat cold ham; said "Think of his calling me a famous liar!"; "I *may*, once in my life—but *he* didn't know anything about *that*."

**29. Sands → Ben, June 12.** "Ant-hill of Chamberlains." Tilly's many acquaintances ("never declining an invitation"). Tilly's marriage plans; decides not to tell Tilly about ferns. "But where am I?" Signed "complete and final disappearance of the Magic Skin."

**30. Ben → Sands, June 13.** Men must withhold things from women; "a rock." Polly tries to open "closets." "Harbour no fear that Polly knows… about the ferns." Obeisance to "Chamberlains."

**31. Tilly → Polly, June 15.** England trip off; Beverley "refuses to tell" the quarrel. "He broke off the engagement." Asks Polly to keep appointment "being loyal!"

**32. Polly → Tilly, June 15.** Excuses herself from Mullen. "The turnip… 'I will not.' 'I will not.'" Polly: "Since I have broken an engagement for you…"

**33. Ben → Polly, June 13 [placed June 15].** Ben spent night with Beverley (window, stars, cigars). Beverley defended Tilly ("white, angelic shape"). Ben: "angel-aeroplane… after more prey." Beverley "suffers." Ben: "I must come to-night."

**34. Polly → Tilly, June 15.** "DEAR, DEAR, DEAR TILLY": asks Tilly to wait until tomorrow; Ben wants to talk.

**35. Polly & Ben (joint, signed both) → Beverley, June 15, late night.** Congratulate broken engagement. Warn: "the love devil… poor quitters."

**36. Tilly → Marigold, June 17.** Third request for bill; refuses his "kindness"; "words not yet uttered."

**37. Tilly → Marigold, June 18.** Remittance. Kentucky cousins sold him a saddle-horse. "Ride like a Kentuckian."

**38. Tilly → Marigold, June 19.** Witnessed his fall ("fell well… not unlike a Kentuckian"). Horse "tricky." Tilly's life story: Kentucky county, six daughters (she in middle: three older, two younger). Father (lawyer) argued suffrage; mother silent, "presenting him with another suffragette." Dolls vs living pets; county fair pets exhibition (kitten, duck, pullet, calf, lamb, puppy); pets sold/killed, replaced. "Long love is possible only when you love often."

**39. Tilly → Marigold, June 21.** He sails tomorrow. Coincidence: he planned pilgrimage to Blackthorne; she was to visit as bride. "Adrift for the summer rather than be an unwilling bride."

**40. Tilly → Beverley, June 21.** Twice before engaged and drew back. "I will live." "For I love you."

**41. Tilly → Polly, June 21.** "Good-bye… for life." Polly keeps furniture/breast-pin unchanged; "soul of perfidy." "Have you confided to Ben… Dr. Mullen?… Or shall I?"

**42. Polly → Ben, June 23.** Worried about Mullen's letters; encloses his letter.

**43. Ben → Polly, June 24 [penciled in Court Room].** Advice: Mullen should enter institution for weak-minded. Returns funeral oration unread.

**44. Ben → Polly, June 24 (evening).** Proposal: "Name the day," "Any day of next Spring." Roses.

**45. Polly → Ben, June 24.** "Oh, BEN, BEN, BEN!" Two rosebuds on pillow.

**46. Ben → Polly, June 26.** Engage Mullen to tell news. "Anything that could sit on his nerves would be a mighty small animal."

**47. Polly → Ben, June 27.** Mullen more determined; "His loyalty is touching."

**48. Ben → Polly, June 28.** Offers Mullen post of furnace-man for one year.

**49. Ben → Polly, July 14.** "I. s. y. s. r. r." Offers to meet Mullen at flat.

**50. Polly → Ben, July 15.** Mullen no longer annoys. "Not an hour these days but my thoughts hover about you."

**51. Sands → Judd & Judd, July 16.** Landscape architects; "any connection with Botany?"

**52. Judd & Judd → Sands, July 17.** No connection with "Botany."

**53. Sands → "Judd & Judd, Per Q.", July 18.** Orders ferns, $25 check; wants to see shipment.

**54. Clara → Sands, July 18.** Father died (weeks ago). Found Burns & Bruce list with his pencilled query. "What a trouble and affliction you have been."

**55. Sands → Judd & Judd, July 21.** Enclosed the list.

**56. Judd & Judd → Sands, July 22.** Cancel original; extra cheque.

**57. Sands → Judd & Judd, July 23.** Encloses cheque.

**58. Sands → Ben, October 30 (1911).** Ferns sailed. Gull on pier. "Le Génie Oblige." "Save me from the things… that look frail and harmless like ferns."

**59. Anne Raeburn → Blackthorne (in Italy), King Alfred's Wood, Nov 30 (1911).** Chronicles. Hodge received hamper of fern-roots from NY; "re-shipped" to forwarders, charges collected in NY. Hodge's ferns: *Scolopendium vulgare*, *Adiantum nigrum*. Dogs wait; smiling tail; pipe. Grand Canal/Venice.

**60. Judd & Judd → Sands, Dec 27 (1911).** Ferns returned, charges due; "ruined and worthless."

**61. Sands → Judd & Judd, Dec 30.** Pays return charges.

**62. Sands → Ben, Dec 28.** "The ferns have come back to me from England!"

**63. Ben → Sands, Dec 29.** "J'y suis, J'y reste." Drop suit against P&F. Fee: $50.

**64. Sands → Ben, Dec 30.** Pays $50 ("damn them"); "That's $75."

**65. Clara → Sands, Dec 25 (1911).** Father fell on library steps, candle on carpet; pneumonia; he had "recollection about a list of ferns." Father believed ferns "most intelligent beings." "You were instrumental in his death."

**66. Clara → Sands, Jan 7 (1912).** Penniless; accepted job at florist Andy Peters' (ex-student of father). Asks Sands to route ferns orders to Peters.

**67. Sands → Ben, Jan 10 (1912).** "I murdered an aged botanist." Clara "harps." Suspects Club trouble: "two wallpaper doctors."

**68. Ben → Sands, Jan 11.** Clara "Great Desert dryness." "Beware of this new Clara!" Humour as nature's solemn gift. Club trouble suspected with "two wallpaper doctors."

**69. Rufus Kent → Sands, The Great Dipper, Jan 12.** Club's "criticism of life," not gossip. Summer 1911 American tourists visited Blackthorne; one asked about Sands; Blackthorne turned curt; at fern spot said "That was once reserved for some ferns which your young American novelist promised to send me." Kent: "your letter is most unbridled." Invites Sands to dinner.

## PART THREE

**70. Clara → Sands, May 1, 1912.** Peters' greenhouse "stifling"; asks if Sands is the novelist; asks inscription "For Miss Clara Louise Chamberlain with the compliments of Beverley Sands." "Your heroine and I are most alike."

**71. Clara → Sands, May 10, 1912.** Owes funeral debt; undertaker. "I now wish I had never spoken of your being instrumental."

**72. Clara → Sands, May 17, 1912.** Thanks for cheque. Peters' "attentions." Wants NY secretary post; "I do love little children."

**73. Clara → Sands, May 21, 1912.** Left greenhouse; Peters "a confirmed rascal."

**74. Sands → Ben, May 24, 1912.** "Clara Louise Chamberlain is in New York! God Almighty!" Gave her cheque. Dictates novels ("organ-grinder"). "Let her be *your* secretary." Encloses address.

**75. Ben → Clara, May 25, 1912.** Job at 10 a.m.

**76. Sands → Ben, May 28.** "What have you done!" Green child in NY.

**77. Ben → Sands, May 29.** Apologetic.

**78. Ben → Sands (inferred)/Ben's hypothetical jury address** (within letter 79 below).

**79. Ben → Sands, May 27 (1912) [in Ben's letter, dictation recap].** Ben dictated mock jury speech to Clara ("adventuress," fine $25, "wiser, better thoughts"). She left address, vanished.

**80. Tilly → Polly, May 30, 1912.** Beverley visits Tilly since breakup. Beverley saw ferns in her vase (roses, white spray, ferns); mutterings "to strange people." Tilly fled upstairs. Second letter enclosed: Marigold called Dr. Mullen; asked Tilly questions about Beverley; asked whether Ben should be told.

**81. Polly → Tilly, June 2, 1912.** Telegram: mother ill in Louisville. "My formidable back is a safe back." Has sent Tilly's letters to Ben.

**82. Polly → Ben, June 2, 1912.** Encloses Tilly's letter. Wants Ben to write daily.

**83. Ben → Phillips & Faulds, June 4, 1912.** Encloses cheque: long-stemmed red roses to Polly.

**84. Ben → Polly, June 4, 1912.** Telegram sympathy. "If Beverley is crazy…" Holds the "key."

**85. Ben → Polly, June 5, 1912.** Mullen visit; dictograph installed by Beverley; Beverley raved about Marigold, Mullen, Ben. Ben invited Mullen, Marigold, their mentors, Club president and two members; Beverley sent to Brooklyn. Uproar; scuffle; door locked. "Beverley's detractors disposed of." P.S.: will "demolish" Blackthorne next.

**86. Polly → Ben, Louisville, June 9, 1912.** Relief Beverley is well. Says Ben's letters "painful shock." "Why should you persecute him because he loved me?" Wedding clothes ordered in Louisville from old mantua-maker. Old Louisville houses "so faithful."

**87. Ben → Blackthorne, 150 Wall St, June 10, 1912.** "I am a stranger to you." Johnson on puppets/Richard III. Novelists' "pedestal" posture; animal types (peacock, owl, porcupine, lamb, bulldog, ass). Three Blackthorne letters; ferns; lied-about character; enclosed brief.

**88. Blackthorne → Ben, June 21, 1912.** Has drawn Ben before: *The Married Cross-Purposes of Ned and Sal Blivvens*; Sal's "shillings" never exact guinea. Son Tommy eats Christmas pudding by piles. "Human cocksure" (Sal Blivvens). Cocksures: rug/floor; Washington and Lincoln; Michael Angelo's *Moses*; Emerson. Admits: "I wronged your friend deeply… a poor, sorry, shabby business." Will write Sands; invite him; write Club president. Denies garden hostility; blames tourists. Robert Burns: "To step aside is human." Hopes Ben never becomes "a broken cocksure."

**89. Ben → Sands, June 30, 1912.** Blackthorne's reply "turned [his letter] into a music-box." "ME—*Sal Blivvens!*" Russians metaphor. Bowed to Marigold and Mullen from car; they smiled. Signed "BEN (alias *Sal Blivvens*)."

**90. Sands → Ben, July 1, 1912.** Voltaire's brother. Ben "not Cassius." Encloses Blackthorne's second letter: Hodge dead ("birthday eclipse"); "mound for… Englishman's ferns"; invites Sands to tea; "two oak trees… meet in their roots." "*Will you, after all, send the ferns?*" "a white light falls on your books."

**91. Judd & Judd → Sands** (catalogue). **P&F → Sands, July 4, 1912** (solicit). **Burns & Bruce → Sands, July 6, 1912** (could ship ferns; "late Noah Chamberlin" a customer; forest trees offered).

**92. Andy Peters → Sands, July 7, 1912.** Business expanded; Clara's "expensive" violet habit; married (wife Alice). "Seedlins… nothing dried."

**93. Ben → Sands, July 7, 1912.** Tilly's marriage announced (to Marigold, "next week"). Ben's own: Polly coming with "wedding clothes." Worried Sands followed Clara: "115 pounds of sealing wax."

**94. Sands → Ben, July 8.** Traced Clara; "royalties are human gratitude."

**95. Meditation in Verse** (dedicated to Ben): refrain "Polly comes with the wedding clothes."

**96. Ben → Sands, July 10, 1912 (hurried).** Polly reached NY two days ago; went out alone; did not return; missing.

**97. Sands → Ben, July 10.** Met Polly on street; she turned back; she was "beautifully dressed." "You will hear."

**98. Sands → Ben, July 11.** Newspaper: "Miss Polly Boles married yesterday at the City Hall in Jersey City to Dr. Claude Mullen." "Oh, Ben, Ben, Ben! So betrayed!"

**99. Diary of Beverley Sands, July 18, 1912.** Tilly's wedding day (to Marigold). Tilly's farewell visit: "Come to-night and say good-bye." Veil scene: "Lift my veil." "Kiss me." She left. Tilly = butterfly seeking perpetual summer; "his" butterfly path. Honeymoon: England, Scotland, France, Switzerland, Austria, Germany, Bohemia, Poland, Russia, Italy, Sicily, then home. Polly's analysis: loyalty; Ben kept Sands's affairs from her; she eloped to City Hall (Justice of the Peace); honeymoon Ocean Grove. Mullen = "pet." Ben stunned; Ben left for Kentucky ("I am going to Kentucky"); expected to marry again, a Polly-like woman. Sands sails for England to visit Blackthorne (house party; critics). Final: "Emblems of Fidelity" — ferns' irony; earth carrying all in one direction. **THE END.**

## Notes on text
- Dates "June 7, 1900" and "June 10, 1900" (P&F/Sands) appear to be typos for 1910.
- Ben's June 13 letter printed after June 15 letters.
- Burns & Bruce letters contain garbled sentences in original.
- Ben's letter to Blackthorne signed "Merely, BENJAMIN DOOLITTLE."
- Clara's father's name spelled "Chamberlin" once (Burns & Bruce July 1912).
